title: Pancreator workflow stage
description: One stage file at library/workflows/<slug>/stages/<stage-slug>.json. A stage is one unit of delegated work with a persona, a task prompt, a workspace mutation policy, a gate, a declared output shape, criteria, and transitions.

slug.description: Stage identifier, unique within the workflow. Must match the file name and appear in the workflow index stages[].

title.description: Human-readable stage name shown on invocation cards and records.

persona.description: Owner of the stage. Resolves to library/personas/<persona>.md and, for delegated work, to the matching .cursor/agents/pan-<persona>.md subagent.

persona_by_verdict.description: Verdict-conditional persona selection. When the latest output of source_stage carries a mapped verdict, the stage runs under the mapped persona instead of its default persona. Run creation validates and snapshots every mapped persona.

source_stage.description: Stage whose latest output supplies the verdict. MUST name another stage in the same workflow.

path.description: Dotted path inside the source output's data object, for example 'verify.verdict'.

map.description: Verdict value to persona name. An unmapped or unreadable verdict keeps the stage's default persona.

evidence_workers.description: Parallel evidence workers the supervisor launches top-level before the stage worker. Each writes one evidence report the stage worker consolidates; submission rejects the stage output while a report is missing.

persona.description: Persona whose projected agent and model mapping the worker runs under.

role.description: Unique evidence dimension slug, for example 'review' or 'qa'.

scope.description: Scope statement rendered into the generated evidence brief.

executor.description: Execution mode. agent delegates to a worker persona. harness runs deterministic runtime logic without delegation.

prompt_path.description: Repository-relative path to the stage task brief. Its contents become the Task section of the invocation card.

workspace_policy.description: Declared mutation expectation. source_allowed may modify product source. release_metadata_only identifies expected self-development release files. runtime_only and read_only normally avoid tracked target changes. For every non-source_allowed stage, scope.no_unapproved_changes detects external or unattributed contamination; worker-attributed internal changes remain visible evidence but do not block.

gate.description: What decides advancement after a successful output. operator: pause for explicit operator approval (intake, ship). supervisor: pause for independent supervisor judgment of the judgment criteria (plan). stage_verdict: the worker's own verdict drives the transition (review, test). next_stage: advance directly to the success transition (implement). An operator-involvement profile MAY replace this gate for a run unless gate_relaxable is false.

gate_relaxable.description: Whether an operator-involvement profile MAY lower this stage's gate. Defaults to true. Set false only where a policy requires the pause to survive configuration, as SHIP-001 does for dev/ship.

checkpoint.description: Role this stage plays for run contracts that attach across workflows. The technical_director contract escalates gates by checkpoint rather than by stage slug, so it applies unchanged to dev/plan, prototype/approach, and design/review. At most one stage per workflow MAY declare a given checkpoint.

context.description: Stage-scoped context projection. Required inputs are read before work; conditional references are opened only on their declared trigger; omitted history remains discoverable through a generated context manifest.

request.description: Whether the original operator request is a required input, a fallback reference, or omitted from the stage card.

required_stage_outputs.description: Effective stage outputs the worker must read. Missing selectors are surfaced explicitly on the invocation card.

conditional_stage_outputs.description: Stage outputs that remain available but should be read only when required inputs do not resolve the task or unresolved remediation evidence requires them.

prior_attempts.description: Maximum prior attempts of the current stage to include as required remediation context.

operator_feedback.description: Maximum recent non-approval remediation notes targeting this stage. Every approval directive targeting the stage remains required input.

include_workspace_ratifications.description: Include the latest operator workspace ratification matching the current fingerprint.

gate_evidence.description: Include a reference to the passed evidence of each repository-check profile a harness gate or baseline already ran, carrying the profile and the workspace fingerprint it passed at, so evidence workers cite the gate instead of re-executing the profile.

required_data.description: Shape contract for the output's data object, as a map of dotted paths to expected JSON types. The harness rejects an output whose data does not match. Type is one of: object, array, string, number, boolean.

criteria.description: Checkable claims for this stage. See governance/criteria/index.md for naming and families.

type.description: judgment: evaluated by a reasoning agent. shell: harness reruns command. state: harness checks run state and fingerprints.

hard.description: If true, failure or not_applicable blocks the stage. Defaults to false.

statement.description: The claim, phrased so that pass is unambiguous.

command.description: Required for type=shell. The exact command the harness reruns; never assembled from agent-controlled values.

timeout_ms.description: Optional timeout for a shell criterion. Defaults to 120000.

transitions.description: Outcome routing. Targets are either another stage slug or a terminal status (succeeded, failed, canceled, paused).

success.description: Target after a successful, gated outcome.

failure.description: Remediation target after a failed outcome (often the implement stage).

blocked.description: Target when the worker reports a blocker; usually 'paused'.

selection.description: latest selects the newest attempt regardless of outcome; latest_success selects the newest successful attempt.
